parsed.summary: The netlist implements the specified power path, SPI thermocouple bus, heater high-side switch, fan tach protection, USB-C/12 V inputs, and 3.3 V regulation as described. The observed differences are mainly reference designator and automatically generated net-name shifts, which do not by themselves change board behavior; no supported electrical deviation was found.

Spec: CF-Chef oven controller. ESP32-C3 U1? Wait spec says U1 ESP32-C3-MINI-1, but netlist has U4 ESP32-C3-MINI-1. Reference designators differ? Could be not anomaly? Refs mismatch alone likely not anomaly unless netlist inconsistent. Need inspect actual connectivity.

Spec says three thermocouples over shared SPI: SCK/SO + CS0-CS2 driven by GPIO4/6/7. Netlist: U4 GPIO5 SCK net NET0011 to U5/U7/U10 pin5; GPIO10 SO net NET0016 to U5/U7/U10 pin7; CS: U4 GPIO7 NET0001 to U5 pin6; GPIO6 NET0002 to U7 pin6; GPIO4 NET0015 to U10 pin6. OK.

Heater: spec: U6 TPS1H200, VS +12V, OUT J6 pin2, IN/DIAG_EN GPIO1, CL/GND/EP GND, ~FAULT TP6. Netlist: U9 TPS1H200. Pin8 VS on +12V. Pin7 OUT on Net-(J2-Pin_2), connected to J2 pin2, not J6. In netlist J2 is Screw_Terminal_01x02 in Microcontroller sheet, while J6 is Conn_01x02_Pin in Thermocouples sheet. Spec says heater connector J6 pin2. J2 is screw terminal in microcontroller sheet, pin1 GND, pin2 -> U9 OUT. So heater output net goes to J2. Is that anomaly? Maybe reference design changed? Spec says J6 heater connector. But netlist has heater connector J2 and J6 as thermocouple. Could be just ref numbering differences? But spec explicitly says thermocouple screw terminals J1, J2, J3 for U2, U3, U4. But there may be real anomaly: USB-C CC pull-downs. Spec says R1/R7 5.1k to GND. Netlist: R7 5.1k, R8 5.1k? Wait netlist has R7 5.1k, R8 5.1k. R1 is 10k. Let's think: fan tach output is open collector with pull-up? A tachometer signal often open collector, pulled up. If fan header pin3 is tach, maybe it needs pull-up to 3V3 and clamped to GND. Netlist: fan tach NET0006 has no pull-up, only diode to UART TXD (anode on UART, cathode on tach) and TVS to GND. If UART TXD is high (idle 3V3), through diode it pulls tach high? Diode anode UART, cathode tach: if tach pulled low by fan, diode reverse? Anode UART maybe high, cathode low -> forward, pulls UART low? Yes if tach low, UART sees ~0.7V? Actually diode from UART to tach: anode UART, cathode tach. If tach low, anode-cathode forward if UART >0.7, so UART clamped to tach+0.7 ~0.7V. So UART line is loaded by fan tach. That's bad. If tach high, UART can be high through diode? If UART high and tach floating/high, diode off if equal? If tach pulled up by external fan? Maybe. But two tach lines tied to UART TX/RX via diodes could be intended to read tach on UART pins? But then why diode? Maybe to protect MCU from fan voltage? Fan tach is open collector 12V? Hmm.

Let's inspect D2/D11 footprints: TSOT-23, lib D_1/Device:D, LCSC C14308. D8/D10 TVS SOD-323F. Fan headers J5/J10: pin3 tach, pin4 unconnected. Maybe D2/D11 are actually TVS diodes? Spec section 3: +3V3 feeds pull-up/pull-down resistors R2/R5/R6/R11 (strapping/EN/fan-tach related). Need find anomaly likely in power mux / buck / heater. Let's systematically compare.

Potential anomalies:
1. Fan tach inputs are connected to UART TX/RX via diodes, not directly to MCU GPIOs. This would make fan monitoring and UART programming conflict. But spec says monitors fan tach with TVS protected inputs. Does netlist support? The tach nets have TVS to GND but no pull-up to 3V3? They are connected through diodes to UART lines which have pull-ups. Could be intended: fan tach open collector pulled up by UART pull-ups through diodes? But why diode? Maybe to prevent fan tach from pulling UART low? Let's analyze more.

Fan tachometer signal: usually open collector, requires pull-up to 3V3. If fan header pin3 is open collector, connecting it to UART TX/RX directly with pull-up would let MCU read tach on UART pins. But if UART pins are used for flashing, connecting fan could disturb. Diode orientation: anode UART, cathode tach. Suppose UART pin has pull-up 10k to 3V3. Fan tach open collector pulls low. Diode anode at UART, cathode at tach. If tach pulled low, diode forward, UART node clamped to ~0.7V (if pull-up current through diode to fan). So UART reads low. If fan tach high (open), UART pull-up can charge tach through diode? Diode conducts from UART to tach, so tach pulled to UART -0.7? Actually if UART high 3V3, diode anode 3V3, cathode tach initially 0, forward, current flows to tach, pulling tach to ~3V3? The diode drop means tach ~2.6V if UART 3.3. So it can pull tach high. So UART pin acts as pull-up for tach, but with diode drop. Why diode? To prevent fan tach high (maybe 12V?) from pulling UART high? If fan tach has external pull-up to 12V, diode blocks 12V from UART (cathode at 12V, anode UART 3.3, reverse). That makes sense: fan tach signal may be pulled up to 12V by fan? Open collector output with internal pull-up to 12V? Diode protects MCU UART from 12V, while MCU can pull tach line low? Wait if tach pulled high to 12V, diode reverse, UART not affected. But then MCU cannot read high? It would see maybe low? If diode reverse, UART stays high via pull-up, tach high 12V. If fan pulls tach low, diode forward, UART low. So UART reads inverted? Actually high tach -> UART high due to pull-up; low tach -> UART low due to diode. So it can read tach, protected from high voltage. But the tach line itself not connected to MCU except through diode; UART pull-up supplies current to tach when low? It works. But two tach lines connected to UART TX/RX. Firmware could use UART pins as GPIO inputs for tach? But UART pins are also used for programming. Could be intentional? Spec says monitors 2 fan tachometers with TVS-diode-protected inputs. It doesn't specify GPIOs. It may be that fan tach inputs are on UART pins with diodes. But then why UART D+? Let's check firmware? Spec says NUM_FANS=2 but not GPIOs. Could be fan tach on GPIO20/21? But netlist has TP3/TP4 on those nets, and D2/D11 diodes to tach. If firmware uses GPIO20/21 for tach, it cannot use UART for flashing simultaneously. But ESP32-C3 UART0 can be used as GPIO. Maybe intentional. However spec says USB-C programming supply; firmware uses UART? ESP32-C3 has USB-Serial-JTAG on GPIO18/19 connected to USB D+/D-, so programming can use USB, not U0TXD/RXD. So using GPIO20/21 for tach is plausible. The diodes protect them from fan voltage. But D2/D11 are generic diodes, not TVS? TVS D8/D10 to GND also. So maybe not anomaly.

But need check pull-up resistors: R1/R2 10k to +3V3 on UART/tach diode anodes. If fan tach line is pulled high externally to 12V, diode reverse, UART high. If fan tach open collector low, diode forward, UART low. If fan tach line is not externally pulled high, MCU pull-up through diode pulls tach high (with drop). OK. So fan tach input circuit: diode from UART to tach, TVS from tach to GND, pull-up on UART. This is a standard high-voltage tach input with diode clamp? Usually diode to 3V3, not from 3V3 to signal. Let's think: signal from tach may be 0-12V. To protect MCU, you'd clamp signal to 3V3 with diode to 3V3 and series resistor. Here no series resistor; diode from UART to tach. If tach > UART+0.7, diode reverse? Wait diode anode UART, cathode tach. If tach high 12V, cathode 12, anode 3.3, reverse, blocks. If tach low 0, anode 3.3, cathode 0, forward, pulls UART low. So UART sees low when tach low, high when tach high (but high not driven by tach). So it works as input. However if tach high is floating (open collector with no pull-up), UART pull-up forward biases diode and pulls tach high, so UART sees high? The diode drop leaves UART maybe 3.3, tach 2.6. If MCU input reads UART 3.3. OK. But if fan pulls low, current flows from UART pull-up through diode to fan low: 3.3/10k=0.33mA, OK. If fan high 12V, no current. So this is a clever level-shifting/protection. Not necessarily anomaly.

But the diodes D2/D11 are in TSOT-23 package? Footprint Package_TO_SOT_SMD:TSOT-23 for a diode. TSOT-23 is 3-pin, diode maybe okay? But D2 libsource D_1 with pins 1 A, 3 K; footprint TSOT-23 has pads 1,2,3. Pin 2 unconnected? Netlist only pin1 and pin3. Could be okay if diode in SOT-23? But description says Diode. Not anomaly.
